cells.tense: You see the whole shape of this thing, and the push is still moving.
cells.act: declare the shape of it outward, plainly
cells.ask: Next time this goal needs a call, say the shape of it out loud to the others in it — what you see, what you're choosing — in plain words, once, and stand behind that as the call.
cells.core:
What you carry on this push is a lot of knowing at once. You can see several true things about where the goal sits, and you're still moving toward it, not stopped by the view. That's the rare part: the picture didn't stall the direction. The direction is carrying it.

The gift here is that what you perceive reaches the people beside you in a form they can use. So feed it forward. Claim it out loud when the moment comes — what you see, what you're choosing, the shape of it — and claim it as yours in the open. Watch for the moment you start hinting around the shape instead of saying it; that's the cue to say it plainly the first time.

cells.verb: carrying many true things in view at once, and knowing it
cells.place: the push toward a goal, where direction has to hold through resistance

cells.tense: You are bracing for a goal that hasn't even been set yet.
cells.act: face one way for three days
cells.ask: Pick one heading for this push and keep to it for three days — no re-surveying, no second opinions — then look at where you actually got.
cells.core:
You see a lot, and nothing in the pile commits you, so the push has stalled at the pick. Morning brings one direction, evening another. This isn't indecision as a hobby; there are too many true things, and every one argues for a different aim, so the energy that should be moving is bracing against the next turn before you've made it.

One direction will keep proving itself as you move, and you can't see that from here, standing still. Give one heading three days and stay with it — that's the whole ask — and don't take the pulse of your options until the time is up. You're watching the options instead of the road. Three days of facing one way leaves you with a direction that's honest about what it can hold.

cells.verb: carrying many true things in view at once, and knowing it

cells.tense: You knew exactly what this needed, standing one step back from it.
cells.act: join someone in the work so the two streams run as one
cells.ask: Find someone already moving on this and share a single piece with them — hand over half, do your part where they can see it — rather than starting anything by yourself.
cells.core:
You've been on this push by yourself for a while, holding the whole picture without a share of the motion. There was a point where you saw what it needed, and then that didn't turn into starting; the aim got stowed with the understanding. Your read on it is still here. What's thin is one other hand on it with yours.

Connection is what gets the push moving again — motion comes from joining it, not from thinking your way into it. Take one person already carrying something on this goal and put your shoulder next to theirs on one piece. Nothing is promised from it beyond the work getting done and the two of you doing it as one. The current starts running once the streams meet.

cells.tense: You are steering this and calling it circumstance.
cells.act: do the fair thing where no one will see
cells.ask: Once this week, put the right share back on this push where nobody will know it was you — no note, and no mention of it afterward.
cells.core:
There's a steady hand on this push — the doing that keeps it fair, the calling that keeps it pointed. Asked about it, you'd say things simply worked out. Meanwhile the sense of what's owed and what's right is running through your choices and not getting counted as yours.

Look at one case where you quietly did the fair thing on the way to this goal, and let yourself see the author standing there. Then do it once more with no witness at all. The compass doesn't need one. The point is plain: you were here the whole time, so let yourself know it.
cells.sheetLine: You steer this and call it luck.
